notes.title: New Update - Curtis, Destructible Objects and More
notes.content:
The new character Curtis is now live.



Changes:

New character Curtis

New physics objects and destructible objects

New boost meter displayed on the HUD with a new option to turn it off

New rail Balance displayed on the HUD with a new option to turn it off

New option to use PlayStation button icons instead of Xbox button icons

New option to change the controller deadzone



I've also launched a new Patreon, subscribe now to help build development funds and increase the development speed.

notes.title: Small fixes 1
notes.content: Fixed small issues and made it so you always start in the middle position on freestyle and time trials.

notes.title: New Map Mars City Mayhem
notes.content:
The new update is finally here! Start playing it now and tell me what you think. I can't wait to hear everyone's feedback!

Changes:

A new level Mars City Mayhem
Radiant Falls visual overhaul and level tweaks
Dream Zone visual overhaul and level tweaks
Maya visual overhaul
Tess visual overhaul
New music
Off axis flips and new rotation code
New option to turn off auto alignment
Physics tweaks and fixes
Ability to rotate between 50-50 grinds and boardslides
Automatically low jump when riding off rails
Increased points gained from spinning without flipping
Increased points gained from board presses
New VFXs
New SFXs
Bug fixes


Updates will come much more frequently going forward. My priority right now is getting more characters and continuing to polish the game's visuals.

notes.title: Next Update Coming May 25!
notes.content:
The next update for Tricky Madness is coming May 25 and it's huge! 🚨

The #1 thing everyone’s been asking for... a NEW MAP: Mars City Mayhem!
It’s a chaotic, city-inspired level that proudly wears its influences on its sleeve. It’s also packed with the most secrets, routes, and unique assets I’ve ever crammed into a map.

Almost all existing content and systems have been reworked. Both characters and both current maps have been updated to fit my new vision for the game. On top of that, in-air rotations have been completely overhauled to look more fluid and allow for off-axis flips. There’s also a new option to turn off auto-alignment with the ground, allowing for smoother flips and spins. 😎

There are a ton of smaller changes too — physics tweaks, grinding improvements, new music, VFX, and SFX.

Thanks so much to everyone who’s supported the game in these early stages. Seriously, it means the world to me. I’ve finally got the systems in place to start adding content more quickly — and honestly, holding all of this for one giant update might not have been the best move.

Going forward, I’ll be rolling out smaller, more frequent updates as new things get finished.

Can’t wait for you to play this one. 💥
— Nathan

notes.title: Physics fixes
notes.content:
Fixed physics playing slower based on frame rate.
Fixed catching air before the end of a ramp.
Fixed Maya's hair glitching out.

notes.title: Physics Changes and Fixes
notes.content:
Holding a left or right when jumping from a rail, will make you jump to that side.
No longer changes your direction when coming off a rail and landing at an angle.
Physics no longer tied to frame rate, fixes some physics bugs.
Fixed settings getting reset.

notes.title: Quick changes
notes.content:
Updated Unity in hopes it will fix some obscure sound and controller issues.
Reduced the DJ's repeat lines frequency.
Fixed a bug where changing difficulty would apply until you relaunched the game.
Made difficulty settings affect the cpu racers more.
